candidates.title: The Elephant Man
candidates.overview: A Victorian surgeon rescues a heavily disfigured man being mistreated by his "owner" as a side-show freak. Behind his monstrous façade, there is revealed a person of great intelligence and sensitivity.
candidates.why: Lynch's most tender nightmare — after Lost Highway and Eraserhead, see where the dream-logic turned heartbreaking.

candidates.title: Baraka
candidates.overview: A paralysingly beautiful documentary with a global vision—an odyssey through landscape and time—that attempts to capture the essence of life.
candidates.why: No plot, no dialogue, just 70mm planet-earth eye candy — your inner Attenborough will eat this up.

candidates.title: Koyaanisqatsi
candidates.overview: Takes us to locations all around the US and shows us the heavy toll that modern technology is having on humans and the earth. The visual tone poem contains neither dialogue nor a vocalized narration: its tone is set by the juxtaposition of images and the exceptional music by Philip Glass.
candidates.why: Life out of balance, scored by Philip Glass — eighty-six minutes of pure hypnotic sprawl.

candidates.title: Fight Club
candidates.overview: A ticking-time-bomb insomniac and a slippery soap salesman channel primal male aggression into a shocking new form of therapy. Their concept catches on, with underground "fight clubs" forming in every town, until an eccentric gets in the way and ignites an out-of-control spiral toward oblivion.
candidates.why: Still unwatched on your own server, and the first rule says we don't talk about why.
